summary: Friday 23 Oct closed the week with US stocks slightly lower (S&P 500 -0.5% on the day and -0.5% on the week; Nasdaq -0.2% and -0.7%) and the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.99%, while chip-equipment names fell hardest: Lam Research -12.8%, KLA -12.2% and Tokyo Electron -11.0% on the week. Brent crude rose about 6% on the week to roughly $117 and WTI to $103.27 as Henry Hub gas fell 15.7% on the week to $2.63/MMBtu; gold lost 4.1% and silver 5.8% on the week. In Asia, South Korea's EWY fund is down 18.5% over the month though SK hynix rose 4.4% on Friday; in emerging markets the Mexican peso weakened 2.2% on the week against the dollar. Turkey cut its policy rate 100 bp to 36% and the Philippines raised its rate 50 bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct, and the Fed (28 Oct), ECB (29 Oct) and Bank of Japan (30 Oct) meet next week. A few items (uranium spot, Kazatomprom, Paladin, Glencore, Air Liquide and palm oil) still carry 22 Oct values (see gaps).

reading.summary: World Shipping Council counts 503 dual-fuel container and vehicle carrier ships in operation as of September 2026, up 41% on a year, with investment above $200 billion.

reading.title: Product Tankers: Less Cargo, Higher Earnings
reading.summary: Broker Xclusiv describes an extraordinary product tanker freight rally from early August to mid-October even as refined product trade contracted.

reading.title: Global shipyard order book grows 13%, strengthening China's lead
reading.summary: BIMCO reports the global order book reached about 203.2m CGT on 1 September, up 13% year on year and just below the May record of 210.4m CGT.

reading.title: Rosatom eyes 2027 for Uzbek large reactor construction
reading.summary: Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said construction of the large units at the planned Uzbek plant is to start in 2027, remarking during a site visit.

reading.title: Radiant microreactor selected for deployment by US Navy
reading.summary: The US Navy chose Radiant's Kaleidos microreactor for deployment at Naval Weapons Station Crane, Indiana.

reading.title: SMRs could be part of Port of Rotterdam's future, says study
reading.summary: A Tractebel and Technopolis study finds the Dutch port could join the SMR supply chain, mainly through non-nuclear components and services.

reading.title: Google and Voltus expand virtual power plant to 1GW in PJM
reading.summary: Google and Voltus agreed to expand their deal to build a virtual power plant totaling 1GW in the PJM region.

overlap.reason: Google is a party to the deal.

reading.title: Peak Energy secures $108m in Series B for sodium-ion battery scale-up
reading.summary: Peak Energy raised $108m in a Series B round to scale manufacturing and deploy its sodium-ion storage systems more widely.

reading.title: Ofgem opens $4.6bn tender for Hornsea 3 offshore transmission assets
reading.summary: Ofgem launched a tender for the offshore transmission assets linking the 2.9GW Hornsea 3 wind farm to the UK grid.

overlap.reason: Hornsea 3 is an Orsted wind farm.

reading.title: Petronas, TotalEnergies, And Mitsui Partner On Offshore Malaysian CO2 Storage Hub
reading.summary: Petronas, TotalEnergies and Mitsui formally signed a joint venture for an offshore CO2 storage hub in Malaysia; the feed excerpt is truncated.

reading.title: Skytree, Galetech, And Mwahera Partner On Direct Air Capture For E-Fuel Production In Kenya
reading.summary: Skytree entered a partnership with Galetech Energy Developments and Mwahera Green Hydrogen on direct air capture for e-fuel production in Kenya.

reading.title: Singapore Pledges $112M For Industrial Decarbonization Research
reading.summary: Singapore will invest S$143 million (nearly $112 million) in research and development to help manufacturers cut emissions.

reading.title: Early speakers' list suggests few powerful leaders will attend COP31
reading.summary: Only 77 heads of state or government are scheduled to speak at the Antalya summit, roughly a third fewer than at COP28.

overlap.reason: Carbon market policy outcomes depend on COP talks.

reading.title: Coal in a green mask: Indonesia's co-firing plan will harm, not help, the climate
reading.summary: Opinion arguing Indonesia's plan to mix wood into coal at power plants could keep coal plants running longer and add pressure on forests.

reading.title: Loss and damage fund agrees $20m for Nepal but rich nations warn it should not set precedent
reading.summary: Board members of the UN loss and damage fund split over whether the Nepal decision should become a model for the fund's long-term work.

reading.title: Death of iconic elephant in Sri Lanka pushes authorities to fast-track protection efforts
reading.summary: Residents of Galgamuwa mourn a wild bull elephant known as Kavantissa; authorities are moving to speed up protection efforts.

reading.title: Indonesians allege social media posts on wildfires and haze are being censored
reading.summary: TikTok removed a Nalar Rawat Institute post on the health effects of Indonesian wildfires; the group says its appeal was rejected.

reading.title: Two Indigenous Brazilians denied their language interpreter at election voting booth
reading.summary: Two Indigenous women who speak only their native language were told only voters with disabilities could get interpreter help in Brazil's Oct. 4 election.

reading.title: Who builds Europe's biggest climate companies #318
reading.summary: Newsletter issue with the teaser "Old World, new founders" on who builds Europe's largest climate companies.

reading.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems gets $85M to build better fusion-ready semiconductors
reading.summary: The startup received an $85 million federal award to advance conductors for fusion power plants.

reading.title: Fusion startup Helion is developing new semiconductors that could double output of its power plants
reading.summary: Helion has another $225 million to speed development of its first fusion power plant, due to supply Microsoft with electricity in 2028.

overlap.reason: Microsoft is the planned power buyer.

reading.title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
reading.summary: GM's fourth-generation EV platform brings a new central computer and electrical architecture, debuting in 2028 in the Cadillac Escalade IQ.

climate.headline: Panama Canal raises draft to 49 ft while preparing for El Nino drought
climate.detail: Authority added a 33rd daily transit slot on 15 Oct and lifted neopanamax draft from 48.5 to 49 ft on good Gatun Lake levels; it is weighing 2027 El Nino measures.
climate.source: Panama Canal Authority announcement, reported by ICIS/Hellenic Shipping News, 2026-09-29 (page dated 2026-10-05)

climate.headline: Copernicus: Western Europe's warmest September, record-low river flows
climate.detail: Western Europe tied its warmest September (+2.51C); record-low September flows on parts of the Rhine, Danube, Vistula and Garonne-Dordogne; late-month flooding in parts of France and Spain.

climate.headline: WMO: El Nino splits Horn of Africa between drought and flood risk
climate.detail: Rain deficits persist in parts of Ethiopia, South Sudan and Sudan, while ICPAC's Oct-Dec outlook is wetter than normal for Kenya, Somalia and southern Ethiopia, with flood and landslide risks.

climate.headline: AFAC: elevated spring bushfire risk in seven Australian states and territories
climate.detail: A very strong El Nino is expected to bring warm, dry spring conditions; southeast NSW, southeast Queensland, northeast Tasmania, and parts of WA, SA, Victoria and the NT are flagged.
climate.source: AFAC spring bushfire outlook, reported by Weatherzone, 2026-08-19

climate.headline: India's monsoon ends 12.6% below normal as northeast monsoon begins
climate.detail: Southwest monsoon withdrew from the whole country on 15 Oct with 759.4 mm against a normal 868.6 mm; northeast monsoon rain began over Tamil Nadu and south India, wet spell expected to 21 Oct.
climate.source: India Meteorological Department, reported by Business Standard, 2026-10-15

indicators.name: US working gas in storage (EIA)
indicators.note: Thursday release for the week ending the prior Friday. The EIA page can return an old cached copy: check that its week-ending date matches the period before recording a value.

indicators.name: Refined copper market balance, year to date (ICSG)
indicators.note: Positive is surplus, negative is deficit, cumulative within the year. Reached through press reports quoting ICSG.

indicators.name: US reactors at 0% power (NRC daily report)
indicators.note: Count of units shown at 0% on the Friday daily report at nrc.gov (URL pattern .../reactor-status/2026/YYYYMMDDps.html). Autumn refuelling pushes the count up. Counted from the page text, so check the count against the page.

indicators.name: Uranium spot price, month-end (Cameco)
indicators.note: Cameco's page lists the month-end spot and long-term price; the long-term price is kept in the note.

spreads.name: Brent minus WTI

spreads.name: Copper to aluminum price ratio
spreads.note: Copper in USD per tonne (pounds converted) divided by aluminum in USD per tonne.

spreads.name: Copper to gold ratio
spreads.note: Copper USD per pound divided by gold USD per ounce, times 1000. A familiar growth-versus-safety gauge.
